piece.caption:
How to stop WhatsApp automation and webhook workflows from crashing during inquiry bursts.

Most automation tutorials test one customer order at a time. In reality, a promotional broadcast or flash sale sends ten inquiries in the same minute. That burst chokes your Google Sheets node and LLM calls, leaving you with dropped rows and half-finished workflow runs. Sheets rate limits usually break first.

The fix is adding a queue step immediately after your webhook trigger. Your flow will process entries sequentially without choking API limits.

Has your sheet or webhook ever skipped inquiries during a sale?

[84] r/automation — what happens to your flow when a trigger sends ten events in a minute
URL: https://www.reddit.com/r/automation/comments/1xefb6t/what_happens_to_your_flow_when_a_trigger_sends/
Most automation tutorials assume one event at a time. Real triggers don’t work like that. An account that posts in bursts can fire a workflow a dozen times in a minute, and the slack node, the google sheets node and the llm call all start choking at different points. Sheets rate limits hit first, usually. A setup that came up recently: a webhook feed from 1322 going into n8n, then a queue step, then the slack message, the sheet row and the llm summary. Before the queue, burst posts caused skipped rows and half finished runs. After it, everything still lands, just a few seconds late. Queue plus
